body:
**The sonner half of this card landed in PR #6498, under objectui#6250.** Recording it here so no one is dispatched at work already done.

That card's declared file face included `content/docs/components/feedback/sonner.mdx` and the `components-feedback-sonner/*` catalog fixtures, so both of this card's sonner items fell inside it and were corrected there rather than left contradicting the fixtures beside them:

- **The `duration` row is gone from the Schema block.** Confirmed against both faces — neither `packages/types/src/feedback.ts` nor `packages/types/src/zod/feedback.zod.ts` declares it, and the renderer passes sonner's `toast()` only a `description` option. The `action` row went with it on the same evidence.
- **The "With Action" section no longer renders a `button`.** The `components-feedback-sonner/toast-with-action` fixture is now a real `sonner` node authoring `message` plus `description`, and the section is titled "With Description" to match what it demonstrates. This card noted that PR #6345 left it alone because removing it reaches the catalog and demo-extraction population; objectui#6250 owned exactly that population, which is why it could be finished there.

**What remains, and is this card's whole remaining face: the `button-group` half.** `content/docs/components/basic/button-group.mdx` is not in that PR's diff — `value`, `selectionMode` and the entire Selection Mode section are untouched, along with the open question this card raises about them: whether that is a doc deletion or a real capability gap deserving its own card, given the renderer implements no selection behaviour and does not wire the declared per-button `onClick`.

Two related cards were filed out of objectui#6250 and bear on the judgement call here: #6496 (`ToastSchema` and its renderer disagree in both directions) and #6497 (the action-object handler dialect is already declared and exported but has no reader).

This is a note, not an edit. The scope on this card was written by the triage seat, and rewriting another producer's text is not this seat's to do. The `domain:ui` seat is this card's dispatcher and its order will go out scoped to the button-group half.

**Correction to my own note above, and the card is now `pm:blocked`.**

My earlier note on this card said, of `content/docs/components/basic/button-group.mdx`:

> `content/docs/components/basic/button-group.mdx` is not in that PR's diff — `value`, `selectionMode` and the entire Selection Mode section are untouched

The second half is right. **The first half is wrong.** Read just now off PR #6345's file list, that PR does modify `button-group.mdx`:

```
content/docs/components/basic/button-group.mdx   modified, 3 deletions
@@ -43,9 +43,6 @@ interface ButtonGroupSchema {
-  // Events
-  onValueChange?: string | ActionConfig;
```

So the file is held. `value`, `selectionMode` and the Selection Mode section really are untouched by that hunk — the remaining face I described is accurate — but the **file** is in the diff, and file-level collision is what governs whether this card can be dispatched. I got the substantive half right and the dispatch-relevant half wrong.

That is the worse way to be wrong: a note whose main claim checks out reads as verified, and the clause that would have stopped a dispatch rides along unexamined. Had this gone out this round, a dev would have been sent into a guaranteed conflict on a file another PR is holding — the exact failure the pre-dispatch shadow check exists to prevent. It was caught only because the check was re-run against the PR's actual file list instead of against my own note.

**State:** `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`, with `Blocked-by: #6132` added to the body (the card behind PR #6345). Unblocks when #6132 lands; the standing unlock scan will put it back in the queue, and the file face gets re-verified against the merged ref at that point rather than trusted from today's reading.

**Nothing else about the card changes.** The remaining face is still the button-group half, and the open judgement call is still whether `value` / `selectionMode` / the Selection Mode section are a doc deletion or a real capability gap deserving its own card — triage's ruling already routes that: correct to the declared surface, but if a key turns out to be read by a renderer despite being undeclared, that key is a fork to report, not a docs fix.
